summary: Alaka Chudal is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD from the University of Vienna (2009–2014). She served as a lecturer at Nepal Sanskrit University (1995–2007) and held a post at the University of Vienna in 2007.

Alan Avdagić works in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena (BA 2019–2023) and the University of Würzburg (MA 2023–2025), holding posts at Würzburg and the Free University of Berlin (attested 2026).
Alan Butterworth (1864–1937) was an Indologist and historian who was educated at Elizabeth College and Balliol College, Oxford, where he studied in 1883.

Alan Coates Bouquet (1884–1976) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at University College London, Trinity College, Cambridge (BA ~1902–1905), and Jesus College, Cambridge. He was Lecturer in History and Comparative Study of Religion at Cambridge (1924–1955).

Alan Entwistle (1949–1996) specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Southampton and SOAS (PhD ~1982 under J. C. Wright) and under Jacob Ensink. He taught at the University of Groningen (1980–1985) and the University of Washington (1986, 1990).

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning a BA from Johns Hopkins (1973–1977) and a PhD from Temple University (1980–1988), he held faculty positions as Professor and Associate Professor at the University of Delaware between 1990 and 2014.

Alan Gerard Wagner specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans (1923–2001) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University, where he studied in 1948 and 1950.

Alan John Bayard Wace (1879–1957) was an archaeologist who studied at Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil. He held positions at the British School at Athens (~1914–1923), the Victoria and Albert Museum (1924–1934), Cambridge (1934–1944), and Alexandria University (~1943–1952).
Alan Lomax (1915–2002) completed studies at Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1933–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).
Alan Nussbaum (1947–) is a linguist and Indologist. He completed his studies at Harvard University (~1969–1976) and was appointed Professor at Cornell University in 1985.

Alan Sponberg (1944–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and taught at Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts (1915–1973) studied religion, philosophy, and Buddhism under D. T. Suzuki, Sokei-an Sasaki, and Dimitrije Mitrinović, receiving a master's from Bexley Seabury. He held posts at Northwestern, the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957), Harvard, and Esalen.

Alasdair MacIntyre (1929–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Manchester. He held academic posts at Essex, Brandeis, Duke, London Metropolitan University, and the University of Notre Dame (~1988–2010).

Alasdair Urquhart (1945–) is a philosopher who earned an MA from Edinburgh and a PhD from Pittsburgh. He served as assistant professor at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Toronto in 1986.

Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who earned a PhD from Cambridge (2009–2013). He held posts at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (2016), SOAS (attested 2019), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Albert Benjamin Norton (1847–1923) was an Indologist and linguist who completed studies at Northwestern University (~1867–1871) and Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary (~1869–1872).

Albert Cuny (1869–1947) was a French linguist who earned his PhD at the Sorbonne, studying under Meillet, Henry, and Lévi. He taught at Lycée Edmond Perrier, held a post at Paris, and was a professor at Bordeaux (1910–1937).

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Basel (1907) under Jacob Wackernagel and Ferdinand Sommer. He held professorships at Greifswald, Bern (1920; 1935–1954), Jena (1925–1935), and taught at Basel (1940–1949).

Albert Esser (1885–1972) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg (Dr.med.), Bonn, and Cologne (PhD under Willibald Kirfel). He served as Privatdozent at Heidelberg (1940) and as Docent and Honorarprofessor at Düsseldorf (1946–1961).
